problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(y)$ has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=4,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3.$ Find $P(y).$
worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=4,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(y-{y}_{1})^{2} & =3{(y-4)}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3{(y-4)}^{2} & =3({y}^{2}-8y+16) \\  & =3{y}^{2}-24y+48.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(y)=3{y}^{2}-24y+48.$
